title: Our Lady of the Rosary (7 October)
hookLine: October is the month of the rosary

lines: IN A POCKET, IN A DRAWER.
cards: Look at the rearview mirror of a taxi in Manila or Mexico City, or in the coat pocket of an old man on a bus in Kraków, and there's a decent chance you'll find a string of beads with a small cross at the end.
Some people pray on it every day. Some carry it and haven't prayed it in years. Some were handed one at a funeral and kept it in a drawer.
On the seventh of October the Church keeps a feast in its name, and the whole month belongs to it.

teach.b: Rosary comes from the Latin rosarium, a rose garden: in the Middle Ages, a garland of prayers was pictured as a crown of roses offered to Mary. The shape grew out of the psalms.

Monks prayed all hundred and fifty; lay people who couldn't read began praying a hundred and fifty Hail Marys or Our Fathers instead, counted on beads or knots. It was sometimes called Mary's psalter.
A popular story says Mary gave the rosary to Saint Dominic. Historians find it taking shape gradually over the centuries instead, and the Dominicans did a great deal to spread it. Then the feast.

On the seventh of October, 1571, the fleet of the Holy League, an alliance Pope Pius V had helped build, met the Ottoman navy at Lepanto, off the coast of Greece. Pius had asked Christians to pray the rosary.
When word came of the victory, he set up a feast of Our Lady of Victory; his successor renamed it Our Lady of the Rosary.
In the 1880s Pope Leo XIII wrote letter after letter about the rosary and gave it the whole month of October.

teach.h: FIVE DECADES, FOUR SETS OF MYSTERIES.
teach.b: The prayer itself is simple: five decades, each an Our Father, ten Hail Marys and a Glory Be, while you think through a mystery from the lives of Jesus and Mary.

Joyful, sorrowful, glorious, and in 2002 John Paul II added the luminous mysteries, from Jesus's public life. The beads keep count so the mind can go somewhere else: to Bethlehem, to the garden, to the empty tomb.

how: Catholics keep the memorial of Our Lady of the Rosary on 7 October and dedicate October to the rosary; many pray it daily that month, alone, as families, or in parish groups, meditating on the joyful, sorrowful, glorious and luminous mysteries.

o: Latin for a prayer book of the psalms
Latin for a string of counting beads
Latin for a rose garden, a garland of prayers

s: historians agree Mary handed the rosary to Saint Dominic
that's a popular story; historians see it taking shape gradually, with Dominicans spreading it.
the 150 Hail Marys mirror the 150 psalms
lay people who couldn't read the psalms prayed a hundred and fifty Hail Marys instead.
the feast was first called Our Lady of Victory
Pius V set it up after Lepanto; his successor renamed it.

games.q: it's 1571. a fleet is sailing toward a great sea battle. you're Pope Pius V in Rome. what do you ask Christians to do?
games.why: he asked for the rosary. after the victory at Lepanto on 7 October he set up the feast that became Our Lady of the Rosary.

practice: Hold beads if you have them, or use your ten fingers, and choose one scene: a birth in a stable, perhaps, or the empty tomb.
If you pray, pray an Our Father and as many Hail Marys as you have time for, keeping the scene in mind; if you don't, move from finger to finger, one breath each, picturing it.

wordCard.voice: rosarium. Latin for a rose garden, the garland of psalms and Hail Marys that grew into the rosary. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: a rose garden — a garland of prayers offered to Mary.

carryVoice: Your line: the month of beads. Ten at a time, a whole October long. Day six hundred eighty-four, done.
